name: Paco
description: Paco is a Mexican gambling rummy closely related to Conquian. Players meld runs and identical-card sets, use forcing to block opponents, and pay the winner based on 'pay cards' (1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 12) melded. A massive 200-card deck made of five Spanish packs allows for sets of identical cards, a key departure from standard rummy.

history.origins: Paco evolved from Conquian in Mexico. Conquian was first documented in Mexico City in 1857 and spread to North America; Paco emerged as its popular gambling variant, played mostly by the older generation.
timeline: Late 1800s: Paco developed as gambling variant with pay-card scoring.
Present: Remains popular in Mexico, especially with older players.
history.cultural: Strong association with Mexican home gambling. The large deck and pay-card system are reminiscent of Panguingue.
history.evolution: Paco added pay-card economics and uses five Spanish 40-card packs. Unlike Conquian, sets must be identical cards (same rank and suit), not just same rank.

setup.players: 2â€“12 players. Deal and play are anticlockwise.
setup.deck: 200 cards from five identical Spanish 40-card packs (suits: swords, clubs, cups, coins; ranks 1â€“7, 10â€“12).
setup.dealing: Ten cards dealt to each player, one at a time. Remainder forms a face-down stock.
setup.equipment: Five Spanish 40-card packs, chips or money for stakes.

rules.objective: Be the first to meld 11 cards in valid combinations. The winner is paid by each opponent according to the 'pay cards' in the winner's melds.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Deal**: Ten cards each. 2. **Cambio**: Each player passes one card face down to the player on their right. 3. **Play**: Each turn, a player may take the card left by the previous player (if it fits a meld) or turn up a new card from the stock. 4. **Melding**: A card taken from the center must be melded immediately with cards from the hand or added to existing melds. It cannot be taken into the hand. 5. **Forcing**: Players can force an opponent to meld the center card if it fits their existing tableau. 6. **Winning**: First to meld an 11th card wins.
keyRules: Valid melds: (1) Run of 3+ consecutive cards in the same suit (7 is adjacent to 10); (2) Set of 3+ identical cards (same rank and suit).
Values: coins=1, cups=2, swords=3, batons=4 pesos per card.
Cards from stock/discard can only be taken if immediately melded.

strategy.basic: Prioritise pay cards (1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 12) when building melds; they translate directly into payment.
strategy.intermediate: Use forcing to disrupt opponents: if the centre card extends an opponent's meld, force it onto them to waste their hand and block their win.
strategy.advanced: Card-count pay cards across the table; avoid leaving key cards where opponents can force you to meld and discard needed cards.
tips: Avoid the 'ten-card hole': if you collect all cards of one suit, you cannot complete a run.
In team play, coordinate with partners on when to force or block.
Identical cards are key for sets; look for duplicates early.

variations.name: Team Paco
variations.description: With 4, 6, 8, etc. players, form two teams. Players sit between opponents. Winning team shares proceeds.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Team play shares proceeds; no engine overrides documented in sources.

scoring.description: Payment is based on pay cards in the winner's melds. Each opponent pays the winner the sum of pay-card values (Coins=1, Cups=2, Swords=3, Batons=4).
scoring.winCondition: First player to meld 11 cards wins the deal and collects from each opponent.
